narr: Clusters of thunderstorms with very high rainfall rates from 2 to 4 inches per hour developed by midday on June 20, and despite being transient, continued to redevelop through the evening and into the overnight hours. The primary focus occurred between Iowa Highway 9 and U.S. Highway 18 as the effective cold pool boundary collapsed southward and locked in place through the night. The final 24 hour rainfall totals reached 6 to 12 inches by daybreak across and near Lyon and northern Sioux counties.
ev: Rainfall reached just shy of 4 inches during the late afternoon and early evening and resulted in numerous streets under water in George and flooding of areas small creeks. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lyon County.

Another 3 to 5 inches of rainfall on top of a similar amount from the earlier afternoon resulted in water flowing across U.S. Highway 75 north of the junction of U.S. Highway 18. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Sioux County.

Flooding of Moon Creek on the west edge of Rock Rapids resulted in evacuations. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lyon County.

An estimated 3 to 4 inches of rainfall between 1 and 4 am CST resulted in significant flooding of creeks and streets near Boyden and Matlock. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Sioux County.
